name: Karl Friedrich Meyer
summary: Swiss-born medical researcher, bacteriologist, and pioneer of disease ecology known for work on zoonotic diseases.

name: Theobald Smith
summary: Comparative pathologist and microbiologist who influenced Meyer's ideas on host-parasite relationships.

name: Frank Macfarlane Burnet
summary: Australian immunologist and Nobel Prize winner who exchanged ideas with Meyer on disease ecology.

name: Charles Elton
summary: British animal ecologist who advised Meyer on the ecology of sylvatic plague.

name: George Williams Hooper Foundation for Medical Research
summary: Medical research foundation at the University of California where Meyer worked and served as director.

name: University of Zurich
summary: Swiss university where Meyer earned his veterinary medicine degree and PhD.

name: University of California, Berkeley
summary: American university where the Hooper Foundation was located and Meyer taught.

name: Veterinary Bacteriological Institute
summary: Research institute in South Africa where Meyer worked as a pathologist.

name: Society of American Bacteriologists
summary: Professional organization where Meyer gave a presidential address on latent infections.

name: South Africa
summary: Country where Meyer worked at Onderstepoort.

name: California
summary: US state where Meyer conducted much of his research on zoonoses.

name: San Francisco
summary: City where the Hooper Foundation was located.

name: Walter Reed Medal
summary: Award for services to tropical medicine received by Meyer.

name: Latent Infections
summary: 1936 presidential address paper by Meyer on latent infections.
